question: Heating ethanol with excess concentrated sulphuric acid produces:
solution:
The correct answer is __**ethene.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethene** is produced when **ethanol **is heated with excess **concentrated sulphuric acid**, which acts as a **dehydrating agent.**
 
• The reaction takes place through an** elimination process**, where a molecule of water is removed from the **ethanol molecule, **resulting in the formation of ethene.
 
• When pure, the gas has a little **"sweet and musky"** smell and is **combustible.**
 
• It is **colorless.**
 
• The **simplest alkene** is this one. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ethanol **is a primary alcohol with the molecular formula C₂H₅OH, commonly used as a **fuel, solvent, and disinfectant.**
 
• **Concentrated sulphuric acid** is a strong acid with the molecular formula H₂SO₄, commonly used in the chemical industry as a **dehydrating agent,** **catalyst, and electrolyte.**
 
• **Ethyne** (acetylene) is a** two-carbon alkyne **with the molecular formula C₂H₂, commonly used in the** welding and cutting industry** as a fuel gas.
 
• **Butane** is a** four-carbon alkane **with the molecular formula C₄H₁₀, commonly used as a** fuel gas in lighters, stoves, and heaters.**
 
• **Ethane** is a **two-carbon alkane** with the molecular formula C₂H₆, commonly used as a **fuel gas and refrigerant.**
